span.p:
EventEnvelope — one shape for every message
event_id · type · review_id
idem_key = review_id, plan_vN and step_id
trace_id ties the event to its span tree
source · ts · payload
this uniformity is what makes tracing,
replay and idempotency work at all

div.style: color: rgb(127, 29, 29) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 460px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Dead letter after five delivery attempts
the review moves to NEEDS_HUMAN and surfaces
as a dashboard card — visible failure handling
is a graded behaviour, so make it visible

div.style: color: rgb(15, 23, 42) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 460px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Ack deadline 60s, extended explicitly
for long model calls

div.style: color: rgb(15, 23, 42) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 460px; text-align: center; width: 460px;

span.p:
At-least-once — and NO ordering guarantee
duplicates are handled by the idempotency key; sequence is handled here.
Every consumer checks review state before acting: a reply after SCORED attaches
as an addendum and reopens the score; evidence.screened before a plan parks and
retries; watchdog.hit deduplicates on signal id; any event for a DECIDED review
appends and never mutates. A decided review is immutable.

svg.text: Drawbridge — Event backbone: agents react to events, they never poll
